overview.title: Overview
overview.description1: This privacy policy explains why we collect your personal data, what we do with it, and your rights. More information about using this service is in the <a routerlink="/terms-and-conditions" href="/terms-and-conditions" >terms and conditions</a >.

whoManagesThisService.title: Who manages this service
whoManagesThisService.description1: This service is managed by Her Majesty’s Courts and Tribunals Service (HMCTS) and we’re responsible for protecting the personal data you provide.
whoManagesThisService.description2: HMCTS is an executive agency of the Ministry of Justice (MoJ). The MoJ is the data controller and their <a href="https://www.gov.uk/government/organisations/ministry-of-justice/about/personal-information-charter" >personal information charter</a > explains more about how they process personal data.
whoManagesThisService.description3: When you use this service we (HMCTS) will ask you to provide some personal data.

whyWeCollectYourPersonalData.title: Why we collect your personal data
whyWeCollectYourPersonalData.description1: We collect your personal data to:
whyWeCollectYourPersonalData.description2: Our staff use your personal data to process your claim or application. They work in the UK and your data is stored in the UK.

typesOfPersonalDataWeCollect.title: Types of personal data we collect
typesOfPersonalDataWeCollect.description1: The personal data we collect includes:
typesOfPersonalDataWeCollect.description2: Some services collect more personal data. Find out more about the <a routerlink="/privacy-policy" fragment="otherservices" href="/privacy-policy#otherservices" >personal data that is collected by the service you are using</a >.

list.item1: your name, address and contact details
list.item2: your email and password (if you create an account)
list.item3: other personal information you provide in your claim or application

usingYourData.title: Using your data
usingYourData.description1: As part of your claim you’ll be asked to use your email address to set up an account. You will be able to use this email and password to sign into other HMCTS services.
usingYourData.description2: We may ask for your permission to use your email address to send you emails using GOV.UK Notify. This system processes emails only within the European Economic Area until the point where emails are handed over to the email provider you use.
usingYourData.description3: We use your personal information in connection with the provision of the IdAM Service. In particular, your personal information may be used for the following purposes:

list.item1: Communicate with you and other individuals.
list.item2: Make assessments and decisions about your identity to manage your access to Services on the Common Platform and maintain information security.
list.item3: Improve the quality of the IdAM Service.
list.item4: Prevent, detect and investigate crime, including fraud.
list.item6: Personalise your experience when you use the IdAM Service.
list.item7: Manage our operations and IT infrastructure, in line with our internal policies and procedures, including those relating to IT systems operation; data and platform hosting; data analytics; business continuity; and records management.
list.item8: Manage complaints, feedback and queries, and handle requests for data access or correction, or the exercise of other rights relating to personal information.
list.item9: Comply with applicable laws and regulatory obligations (including those outside your country of residence); comply with legal process and court orders; and respond to requests from public and other government authorities (including those outside your country of residence).
list.item10: Establish and defend legal rights to protect our operations and secure our and your rights, privacy, safety or property, and those of other individuals or third parties; to enforce our terms and conditions; and pursue available remedies or limit our damages.

storingYourData.title: Storing your data
storingYourData.description1: When you make your claim or application we store the data you have provided. The amount of time that your data is kept for depends on the service that you are using.
storingYourData.description2: When you make your claim or application we store the data you have provided. The amount of time that your data is kept for depends on the service that you are using.
storingYourData.description3: Some services collect more personal data. Find out more about the <a routerlink="/privacy-policy" fragment="otherservices" href="/privacy-policy#otherservices" >personal data that is collected by the service you are using</a >.

sharingYourData.title: Sharing your data
sharingYourData.description1: While processing your claim or application, another government department, agency or organisation might be involved and we may share your data with them.
sharingYourData.description2: If you contact us and ask for help with the service you are using, your personal data may be shared with the Good Things Foundation. This is a company who we have partnered with to offer face to face support.
sharingYourData.description3: In some circumstances we may share your data for example, to prevent or detect crime, or to produce anonymised statistics.
sharingYourData.description4: We use Google Analytics to collect data about how a website is used. This anonymous data is shared with Google. Find out about this in our terms and conditions.

storingAndSharingYourDataInternationally.title: Storing and sharing your data internationally
storingAndSharingYourDataInternationally.description1: Sometimes we need to send your personal information outside of the UK. When we do this we comply with data protection law.

yourRights.title: Your rights

list1.item1: to see the personal data that we hold on you
list1.item2: to have the personal data corrected
list1.item3: to have the personal data removed or deleted (this will depend on the circumstances, for example if you decide not to continue your claim or application)
list1.item4: that access to the personal data is restricted (for example, you can ask to have your data stored for longer and not automatically deleted)

yourRights.description2: If you want to see the personal data that we hold on you, you can:

list2.item1: writing to us: Data Protection Team, Ministry of Justice, 11th Floor, Post Point 11.52, 102 Petty France, London SW1H 9AJ
list2.item2: write to us: Data Protection Team, Ministry of Justice, 11th Floor, Post Point 11.52, 102 Petty France, London SW1H 9AJ

yourRights.description3: You can ask for more information about:

list3.item1: agreements we have on sharing information with other organisations
list3.item2: when we are allowed to pass on personal information without telling you
list3.item3: our instructions to staff on how to collect, use or delete your personal information
list3.item4: our instructions to staff on how to collect, use or delete your personal information

yourRights.description4: You can contact the MoJ data protection officer, by:

list4.item1: how we check that the information we hold is accurate and up-to-date

howToComplain.title: How to complain
howToComplain.description1: See our <a href="https://www.gov.uk/government/organisations/hm-courts-and-tribunals-service/about/complaints-procedure" >complaints procedure</a > if you want to complain about how we’ve handled your personal data.
howToComplain.description2: Write to: Data Protection Team, Ministry of Justice, 11th Floor, Post Point 11.52, 102 Petty France, London SW1H 9AJ
howToComplain.description4: You can also complain to the Information Commissioner’s Office if you’re not satisfied with our response or believe we are not processing your personal data lawfully.

theServiceYouAreUsing.title: The service you are using
theServiceYouAreUsing.description1: The types of personal data collected, how long it is stored for, and who it is shared with depends on the service you are using. Find out more by following the links below:

usingTheAppealABenefitDecisionService.title: Using the appeal a benefit decision service

thePersonalDataWeNeed3.title: The personal data we need
thePersonalDataWeNeed3.description1: When you use the appeal a benefit decision service we ask for:

list1.item3: your email or mobile phone number
list1.item5: information from the Mandatory Reconsideration Notice
list1.item6: information on any support you need for a hearing, if you attend one
list1.item7: information on your availability for a hearing, if you attend one

thePersonalDataWeNeed3.description2: If you have a representative, we will ask for:
thePersonalDataWeNeed3.description3: If you are appointee, you will need to provide information about the person who you are appealing on behalf of, including:

receivingNotifications2.title: Receiving notifications
receivingNotifications2.description1: As part of your appeal we’ll ask if you want to receive text message and email notifications to keep you updated with your appeal.
receivingNotifications2.description2: You can cancel text messages by following the steps mentioned in the text message, and you can cancel emails by following the steps mentioned in the emails.
receivingNotifications2.description3: If you have asked for your named representative to receive updates on your appeal, then we will share your data with them. If you want your representative to stop receiving notifications then you need to Contact us.

storingAndSharingYourData.title: Storing and sharing your data
storingAndSharingYourData.description1: Your data will be shared with the government department that made the decision you are appealing against. For example, the Department for Work and Pensions or HM Revenue and Customs. This is so that department can respond to your appeal.
storingAndSharingYourData.description2: After you complete your application it will be stored for 2 years. It will be deleted after that.

usingTheApplyForADivorceService.title: Using the apply for a divorce service

thePersonalDataWeNeed.title: The personal data we need
thePersonalDataWeNeed.description1: When you use the apply for divorce service we need the following personal data:

list.item2: your name on the marriage certificate
list.item3: a copy of your marriage certificate
list.item5: country in which you got married
list.item6: information about where you have lived
list.item7: your habitual residence (whether your life is mainly based in England or Wales)
list.item8: your domicile (usually the place in which you were born, regard as your permanent home and to which you have the closest ties)
list.item9: your email or mobile phone number
list.item12: to know if you have been involved in other court cases
list.item13: your husband or wife’s current name
list.item14: their name on the marriage certificate
list.item15: the name and address of the person who committed adultery with your husband or wife (this is optional and only asked if adultery is your reason for divorce)
list.item16: your solicitors name and address (if you have one)

receivingNotifications.title: Receiving notifications
receivingNotifications.description1: You need to sign up to receive notifications to use the apply for divorce service. This is a legal requirement so that the divorce application can proceed.

storingYourData2.title: Storing your data
storingYourData2.description1: When you use this service you’ll be asked to use your email address to set up an account. You will be able to use this email and password to sign into other HMCTS services.
storingYourData2.description2: While you are filling out or responding to a divorce application we will hold your data for up to 6 months. If you don’t complete the application during this time you’ll have to start again.
storingYourData2.description3: When a divorce is finalised the case is stored for 18 years. After this time, some data (from the decree nisi and the decree absolute) is deleted.
storingYourData2.description4: The remainder of the case information is stored for an additional 82 years. After a total of 100 years this data will be deleted.

sharingYourData2.title: Sharing your data
sharingYourData2.description1: While processing your claim or application, another government department, agency or organisation might be involved and we may share your data with them.
sharingYourData2.description2: Any data you provide which needs to be printed will be shared with Xerox (UK) Ltd. For example, the divorce application will be printed so that it can be sent to the respondent by post.
sharingYourData2.description3: Any data which is posted in to support a divorce application will be shared with Exela Technologies Limited. For example, a posted marriage certificate will be received by Exela and sent to the court as a scanned image.
sharingYourData2.description4: If you contact us and ask for help with the service you’re using, your personal data may be shared with the Good Things Foundation. This is a company who we have partnered with to offer face to face support.
sharingYourData2.description5: In some circumstances we may share your data for example, to prevent or detect crime, or to produce anonymised statistics.

usingTheApplyForProbateService.title: Using the apply for probate service

thePersonalDataWeCollect.title: The personal data we collect
thePersonalDataWeCollect.description1: When you use the apply for probate service we ask for:

list.item1: your name, and any other names you are known as
list.item5: the names of any executors of the will
list.item6: contact details for all of the executors who are applying for probate

storingYourData4.title: Storing your data
storingYourData4.description1: As part of your application you’ll be asked to use your email address to set up an account. You will be able to use this email address and password to sign into other HMCTS services.
storingYourData4.description2: We may ask for your permission to use your email address to send you emails using GOV.UK Notify. This system processes emails only within the European Economic Area until the point where emails are handed over to the email provider you use.
storingYourData4.description3: We use cookies to collect data that tells us about how you’re using this service, including:

list.item1: if you open an email from us or click on a link in an email
list.item2: your computer, phone or tablet’s IP address
list.item3: the region or town where you are using your computer, phone or tablet

storingYourData5.title: Storing your data
storingYourData5.description1: When you use this service you’ll be asked to use your email address to set up an account. You can use this email address and password to sign into other HMCTS services.

beforeYouSubmitYourInformation2.title: Before you submit your information
beforeYouSubmitYourInformation2.description1: Information you enter in the apply for probate service is saved until you decide to submit it. This allows you to save what you are doing and continue later. Saved information that you do not submit will be deleted after 180 days.

afterYouSubmitYourInformation2.title: After you submit your information
afterYouSubmitYourInformation2.description1: Information you enter in the apply for probate service will be stored for 50 years and then deleted. Wills and grants of probate can be accessed as public records. Grants of probate do not include email addresses and telephone numbers, but they do include addresses.

sharingYourData4.title: Sharing your data
sharingYourData4.description1: While processing your application, another government department, agency or organisation might be involved and we may share your data with them.
sharingYourData4.description2: If you contact us and ask for help with a service you are using, your personal data may be shared with the <a href="https://www.goodthingsfoundation.org/" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" >Good Things Foundation (opens in a new window)</a >. This is a company who we have partnered with to offer face to face support.
sharingYourData4.description3: In some circumstances we may share your data. For example, to prevent or detect crime, or to produce anonymised statistics.
sharingYourData4.description4: We use Google Analytics to collect data about how a website is used. This anonymous data is shared with Google. Find out about this in our terms and conditions.
sharingYourData4.description5: Storing and sharing your data internationally
sharingYourData4.description6: Sometimes we need to send your personal information outside of the UK. When we do this we comply with data protection law.

thePersonalDataWeNeed2.title: The personal data we need
thePersonalDataWeNeed2.description1: If you are using the money claims service we will ask you for:

list1.item2: your business or organisation if you are acting on their behalf
list1.item4: your email or mobile phone number
list1.item6: the name of the person, business or organisation you are claiming against
list1.item9: the reasons you are making the claim
list1.item10: the timeline of events leading to the dispute
list1.item11: a list of any evidence you have to support your claim

thePersonalDataWeNeed2.description2: If you are responding to a money claim we ask you to check the personal information about you that was provided by the claimant which includes your name, your address and contact details.
thePersonalDataWeNeed2.description3: We may ask you to provide:

list2.item2: your business or organisation if you are acting on their behalf
list2.item3: your response to the claim made against you
list2.item4: the timeline of events leading to the dispute
list2.item5: a list of any evidence you have to support your claim

storingYourData3.title: Storing your data
storingYourData3.description1: When you use this service you’ll be asked to use your email address to set up an account. You can use this email and password to sign into other HMCTS services.

beforeYouSubmitYourInformation.title: Before you submit your information
beforeYouSubmitYourInformation.description1: The information you enter in the money claims service is saved until you decide to submit it. This allows you to save what you are doing and continue later. Saved information that you do not submit will be deleted after 90 days.

afterYouSubmitYourInformation.title: After you submit your information
afterYouSubmitYourInformation.description1: The information you submit for a money claim will be deleted 2 years after the court makes a decision on the outcome of your claim (this is called a judgment).
afterYouSubmitYourInformation.description2: If the court doesn’t make a decision about your claim (for example, you settle the claim out of court and a judgment is no longer required) then the information you provide will be deleted 3 years after the last update made to the claim.

sharingYourData3.title: Sharing your data
sharingYourData3.description1: The information you submit will be shared with everyone who is named on the claim. This excludes any payment details that you use to pay court fees.
sharingYourData3.description2: If a judgment is made on a case some information is shared with Registry Trust Limited who provide financial information about court judgments to banks and credit agencies.
sharingYourData3.description3: Any data posted in by you or other parties to support the claim issue and progression will be shared with Exela Technologies Limited and, if printing is required, with Xerox (UK) Ltd.

usingTheFamilyPublicLawService.title: Using the family public law service

whatIsThePersonalDataThatWe.title: What is the personal data that we collect
whatIsThePersonalDataThatWe.description1: When you use the Family Public Law service, we collect the following personal data:

list1.item1: the applicant’s name, address, job role and contact details
list1.item2: the Local Authority solicitor’s name, address and contact details
list1.item3: the social worker’s name, address and contact details
list1.item4: name, date of birth, gender, and address of children in the case
list1.item5: name, date of birth, gender, address and contact details of respondents in the case
list1.item6: name, address and contact details of other parties in the case, for example witnesses
list1.item7: details of any disability or litigation capacity (ability to understand proceedings) of any child, respondent or other party in the case
list1.item8: details of other court cases respondents or children in the case have been involved in

list2.item1: information that tells us if you open an email from us, or click on a link in an email
list2.item2: information about how you use this service, like your IP address and the web browser you use. We do this by using cookies

whatWeDoWithYourData.title: What we do with your data
whatWeDoWithYourData.description2: Personal data is processed by our staff in the UK and the data is stored in the UK.
whatWeDoWithYourData.description3: Data relating to a case is stored until the youngest child reaches 18 years old, unless the case results in adoption where the data is stored for 100 years.
whatWeDoWithYourData.description4: We use GOV.UK Notify to send emails. These are processed within the EEA until the point where emails are handed over to your email provider.

yourRights2.title: Your rights
yourRights2.description2: Email data.access@justice.gov.uk if you want to see any of this information.

list.item1: to see the personal data that we hold on you
list.item2: to have the personal data corrected
list.item3: to have the personal data removed or deleted (this will depend on the circumstances, for example if you decide not to continue your claim or application)
list.item4: that access to the personal data is restricted (for example, you can ask to have your data stored for longer and not automatically deleted)

sharingYourData5.title: Sharing your data
sharingYourData5.description1: We allow Google to use or share our website analytics data, find out about this in our  <a routerlink="/terms-and-conditions" href="/terms-and-conditions" >terms and conditions</a >.

receivingNotifications3.title: Receiving notifications
receivingNotifications3.description1: As part of your application we will send you notifications to let you know how your application is proceeding.
receivingNotifications3.description2: Email contactfpl@justice.gov.uk if you want to cancel email updates.

howToComplain2.title: How to complain
howToComplain2.description1: If you want to complain about how we have handled your personal data, email DataProtection@justice.gov.uk.
howToComplain2.description2: You can complain to the Information Commissioner’s Office if you are unsatisfied with our response or believe we are not legally processing your personal data.

usingTheAppealAnImmigrationOrAsylum.title: Using the Appeal an immigration or asylum decision service

thePersonalDataWeNeed4.title: The personal data we need
thePersonalDataWeNeed4.description1: When you use the appeal an immigration or asylum decision service we ask for:

list.item4: your email or mobile phone number
list.item7: information from the Home Office decision letter
list.item8: information on any support you need for a case management appointment or hearing, if you attend one

storingAndSharingYourData2.title: Storing and sharing your data
storingAndSharingYourData2.description1: Your data will be shared with the government department that made the decision you are appealing against. For example, the Ministry of Justice. This is so that the department can respond to your appeal.

afterYouSubmitYourInformation3.title: After you submit your information
afterYouSubmitYourInformation3.description1: The information you submit will be deleted 2 years after the Tribunal has issued its decision and the last update has been made to your appeal.
afterYouSubmitYourInformation3.description2: If the Tribunal doesn’t make a decision about your appeal (for example, it is withdrawn, or both parties agree) then the information you provide will be deleted 2 years after the appeal has been closed and the last update made.
afterYouSubmitYourInformation3.description3: If you make a complaint against the Tribunal then information about the appeal is stored for 3 years after the last update on the complaint.

thePersonalDataWeNeed5.title: The personal data we need
thePersonalDataWeNeed5.description1: If you are using the possession claims service we will ask you for:

list1.item1: your name or the name of your business or organisation
list1.item2: your email or mobile phone number
list1.item4: the address of the property you are seeking possession of
list1.item5: the name of the person, business or organisation you are claiming against
list1.item7: the reasons you are making the claim
list1.item8: evidence you have to support your claim

thePersonalDataWeNeed5.description2: If you are responding to a possession claim we ask you to check the personal information about you that was provided by the claimant which includes your name, your address and contact details.
thePersonalDataWeNeed5.description3: We may ask you to provide:

list2.item2: your business or organisation if you are acting on their behalf
list2.item3: your response to the claim made against you
list2.item4: evidence you have to support your claim

storingYourData6.title: Storing your data
storingYourData6.description1: When you use this service you’ll be asked to use your email address to set up an account. You can use this email and password to sign into other HMCTS services.

beforeYouSubmitYourInformation3.title: Before you submit your information
beforeYouSubmitYourInformation3.description1: The information you enter in the possession claims service is saved until you decide to submit it. This allows you to save what you are doing and continue later. Saved information that you do not submit will be deleted after 30 days.

afterYouSubmitYourInformation4.title: After you submit your information
afterYouSubmitYourInformation4.description1: The information you submit for a possession claim will be deleted 6 years after the court makes a decision on the outcome of your claim.
afterYouSubmitYourInformation4.description2: If the court doesn’t make a decision about your claim (for example, you settle the claim out of court) then the information you provide will be deleted 3 years after the last update made to the claim.

sharingYourData6.title: Sharing your data
sharingYourData6.description1: The information you submit will be shared with everyone who is named on the claim. This excludes any payment details that you use to pay court fees.
sharingYourData6.description2: Any data posted in by you or other parties to support the claim issue and progression will be shared with Exela Technologies Limited and, if printing is required, with Xerox (UK) Ltd.
